headline: Visayas Grid Under Red and Yellow Alerts as Major Power Units Remain Offline
seoTitle: Visayas Grid Under Red, Yellow Alerts August 25 | FMB News
seoDescription: NGCP placed the Visayas grid under red and yellow alerts on August 25 as major generating units remained unavailable and capacity fell below peak demand.
deck: NGCP scheduled a red alert for the evening peak and yellow alerts around it as available capacity remained below projected demand.
author: FMB News Desk

sections.heading: What happened
paragraphs: The National Grid Corporation of the Philippines placed the Visayas grid under a red alert from 5 p.m. to 8 p.m. Tuesday, August 25, with yellow alerts scheduled before and after the evening peak.
NGCP reported available capacity of about 2,421 megawatts against projected peak demand of about 2,570 MW.

sections.heading: Context
paragraphs: Current PNA reporting identifies the unavailability of major Therma Visayas and Kepco SPC units among the key constraints. NGCP reported about 904.5 MW unavailable across forced outages and derated plants, a larger total than the 450-MW figure in the approved email summary.

sections.heading: Why this matters
paragraphs: A red alert means supply is insufficient to meet demand and the grid's regulating requirement, increasing the risk of service interruptions if additional supply or demand-side measures are not available. A yellow alert means reserves are below contingency requirements.

sections.heading: What to watch next
paragraphs: Watch NGCP and the Department of Energy for updated alert windows, restoration of generating units and any demand-management measures during the evening peak.
